title: Architecture Guide
description: Comprehensive guide to core vs. overlays, controller-service-repository patterns, route handling, theme/constants management, and prisma schema merging.

blocks.text: This guide provides maintainers with in-depth knowledge of how the template engine is designed. By understanding these concepts, you can easily develop new components, modify core features, or create new template overlays.
To serve different clients (e.g. Hotel website vs. Real Estate portfolio) without duplicating infrastructure, the codebase is split into reusable core code and client-specific overlay modifications.

items: Core (packages/core): Contains base boilerplate, authentication system (Auth.js), lead storage, admin portal, basic styling templates, and standard API routers.
Overlays (templates/overlays/): Contains custom page templates, landing page overrides, brand-specific configurations, styles, and custom Prisma models that overwrite or extend the core code.

Synchronization (pnpm sync-templates): The sync script (scripts/sync-templates.mjs) builds a fresh template by copying core first, applying the overlay on top (overwriting duplicate paths), and merging Prisma schemas.

blocks.title: Maintainers Warning
blocks.text: Maintainers must never edit directories under templates/* directly (such as templates/hotel-website-template). These directories are generated by the sync script, and any changes made directly there will be permanently overwritten next time the sync task is executed.

Domain-specific backend features are organized under lib/features/<domain>/ following a strict Controller-Service-Repository separation of concerns. This ensures modularity, clean testing interfaces, and easy maintainability. An example implementation is lib/features/leads:
The repository layer is the only layer that directly communicates with the database via the Prisma client. It abstracts database query operations (e.g. findMany, create, update).

The service layer contains core business logic, input validation, sanitization, and data transformations. It is independent of HTTP details and depends entirely on the repository layer. For example, verifying 10-digit mobile numbers or formatting email inputs is handled here.

The controller layer acts as the bridge between HTTP transport and business logic. It extracts request bodies, handles exceptions, returns JSON responses (NextResponse) with appropriate status codes, and is injected with the service layer.

Next.js App Router route handlers (app/api/<feature>/route.ts) act as entry points. They check session credentials (where authorization is required) and immediately forward the request to the controller. This keeps the routing files thin and easily readable.
All branding, contact details, SEO, and visual design values live in constants/site.ts inside the template overlay directory. This acts as the single source of truth for the entire template.

items: SITE.brand: Name, shortName, tagline, managedBy, and copyright text.
SITE.contact: Phone, Display Phone, Whatsapp, Country Code, Email, and physical addresses.
SITE.seo: SEO default page titles, description, keywords, prices, and schema schemas.
SITE.theme: CSS colors (primary, primaryHover, accent, accentDark, textMain, textMuted, bgMain, bgLight, etc.) used to style buttons, headers, borders, and backgrounds dynamically.

blocks.text: Components retrieve these settings dynamically (e.g. style={{ backgroundColor: SITE.theme.colors.primary }}). This enables maintainers to change the branding or colors of the entire website by editing a single config file.

Next.js templates require database operations. Instead of duplicating schemas, the core schema (packages/core/prisma/schema.prisma) defines standard models like Lead and PromoBanner. Client overlays define domain models (e.g. RoomType or Project). During compilation, the merge script combines these models into one consolidated schema.prisma file, removing duplicated preambles and shared models.
